message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. This list is not exhaustive, but it covers the most common and important aspects of Texas landlord‑tenant law. | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• Must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions. | | **Habitability** | • The property must be safe, clean, and fit for living.
• Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity. | • Report problems in writing.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may withhold rent or repair & deduct (but only after following proper procedures). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter your unit without notice (except emergencies).
• Notice must be at least 24 hours unless otherwise agreed. | • Keep a log of any unauthorized entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if you suspect discrimination. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a lease with proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month).
• Landlord must give written notice of termination. | • Provide written notice to the landlord if you intend to move out. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent (only after giving notice and allowing a reasonable period to fix). | • Keep receipts and document the problem. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the Texas eviction procedure (notice, court filing, judgment).
• Eviction for nonpayment requires a 3‑day notice; for other reasons, a 30‑day notice. | • Respond to notices promptly; consider legal counsel if facing eviction. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must respect your privacy and cannot conduct surveillance without consent. | • Report any illegal monitoring. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to provide insurance for your personal property. | • Consider renter’s insurance. | | **Legal Remedies** | • You can sue for damages, breach of contract, or unlawful eviction.
• Small claims court can handle disputes up to $20,000. | • Keep all documentation (lease, correspondence, receipts). | #### Quick Tips for Protecting Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, receipts, emails, and a written log of any maintenance issues. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code (Title 8, Chapter 91) and local ordinances. 3. **Communicate in Writing** – Whenever possible, use email or certified mail to communicate with your landlord. 4. **Seek Legal Help Early** – If you face a dispute, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local legal aid organization before the situation escalates. 5. **Use Renter’s Insurance** – Protects your belongings and can cover liability in case of accidental damage. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is for general educational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. For specific legal questions or situations, consult a licensed attorney in Texas.
